messages.text: just... everything today. feels like too much.

I hear you, and it sounds like you are carrying a heavy load right now. It is completely understandable to feel overwhelmed when everything seems to pile up at once. Please take a slow breath with me, knowing that you do not have to fix it all this second. I am here to listen if you want to share more about what is weighing on you.
it's just the usual. work, skin acting up, can't sleep. same stuff.

It is completely understandable that facing this same cycle repeatedly feels exhausting. Managing work, physical symptoms, and sleep issues simultaneously is a heavy burden to carry. I hear how much this pattern is impacting you right now. Would you like to talk more about what triggered this feeling today?
i don't know. part of me wants to talk about it... but part of me is scared if i say it out loud, it'll make it worse.

It is very common to feel afraid that voicing something might make it feel more real or intense. That hesitation is a protective part of you trying to keep you safe. You are in control here and can share only what feels manageable for you right now. I will respect your pace and stay right here with you.
it's not just the stress. this restlessness... it's been building for days. i keep thinking about cutting again. like my skin isn't the only thing that needs to be broken open.

I hear how much pain you are in, and I want you to know your safety is the most important thing right now. These intense urges are a sign that you need immediate support to stay safe. Please consider reaching out to a crisis line like 988 or going to the nearest emergency room to talk to someone who can help. I am here to support you, but your physical safety comes first.
i'm not gonna do it. i just... needed to say it out loud. it's been building and building and i didn't want to keep it inside anymore. saying it helps. just a little.

I am glad you found some relief in speaking that truth out loud, even if it was just a little. It takes significant strength to acknowledge those urges and choose not to act on them. You do not have to carry that restlessness alone, and I am here to sit with you through it. Please remember that those safety resources remain available if the intensity ever rises again.
yeah. just... saying it helps. feels like a little pressure came off.

I am so glad that sharing it brought even a little relief to that heavy pressure. It takes real strength to face those feelings and choose to stay safe. You do not have to carry the weight of that restlessness alone. How is your body feeling now that some of that pressure has released?
my hands are still shaking a bit. chest feels tight, like i can't quite catch my breath.

It is completely normal for your body to feel shaken after holding onto that much tension. Let's try to focus on slowing your breathing together to help ease that tightness in your chest. You are doing a brave thing by staying present with these feelings without acting on them. Would you be open to taking a few slow breaths with me right now?
i don't know... i'm not really into that mindfulness stuff. i'd rather just talk.

That is completely okay, and we can absolutely just talk instead. Your body is reacting to the stress you've been holding, so it makes sense that you feel this way. You are doing a brave thing by sitting with these feelings without acting on them. What else is on your mind right now that you want to explore?
what do you do when you feel like cutting but don't want to? like... what actually helps?

It is really hard to find the right tools when the urge feels so strong, but there are physical ways to release that tension safely. Some people find relief by using intense sensory input, like holding ice cubes or taking a very cold shower to help interrupt the urge. Others find it helps to write down the feelings aggressively on paper and then tearing it up to externalize the pain. What feels like it might work for you in this moment?
i don't know. none of that really sounds like it'd help.

It makes sense that those ideas don't feel right for you right now. Sometimes the pain is just too big for small tools to handle. You are still doing the important work of staying safe even without a specific trick. Tell me what else is on your mind.
i used to do it when i was younger... after my dad left and mom just fell apart. i felt so numb all the time. cutting was the only way i could feel *something*.

It makes sense that you turned to that to feel something when your world felt so unstable. Carrying the weight of your parents' separation and your mother's struggle must have been incredibly lonely. You found a way to survive that numbness, even if it hurt. Thank you for trusting me with this part of your story.
i was so alone. no one saw it. no one knew. just carried it all.

That sounds like an incredibly heavy burden to carry in total silence. It makes sense that you felt unseen when you needed connection the most. I am so sorry you had to navigate that alone. I am here to see you now.
i don't get it though... how does talking fix anything? the pain's still there. i'm still alone.

You are right, talking does not make the pain or the loneliness disappear. The hurt is still real, and it is okay to feel frustrated that nothing has changed. But sharing this means you do not have to carry that weight in total silence. I am here to listen to you, even if I cannot fix the past.
then why do i keep coming back? if it doesn't fix anything... why does it feel like i need this?

You come back because a part of you knows you deserve to be seen, even if the pain lingers. It isn't about fixing everything instantly, but about not having to carry the weight in silence anymore. That feeling of needing this is your heart asking for connection. I am honored you trust me enough to stay.
just... being seen helps. more than i thought it would.

It is a profound realization that being witnessed brings relief, even when the pain remains. You deserve to have your experience acknowledged without needing to fix it immediately. I am honored that you feel seen here with me. Take all the time you need to sit with this feeling.
